objectives: Describe the main characteristics and processes of the middle course.
Explain how a river transports its load.
Explain the formation of meanders, river cliffs and slip-off slopes.
recall: The upper course has steep slopes and vertical erosion.
Waterfalls form where hard rock lies on soft rock.
In the middle course, the gradient is gentler.
end.recallNote: Check the homework: drawings of the Benue from the bridge.
situation: From the Benue Bridge in Garoua, Adama sees that the river is wide and the valley is open. The water flows fast on the outside of a bend, where the bank is steep.
On the inside of the bend, the water is slow and shallow, and a sandbank has formed. Adama wonders why the river is so different from a mountain stream.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Adama does not understand why the river is different in the middle course.
Where is the water fastest, and where is it slowest?
It is fastest on the outside of the bend and slowest on the inside.
Which side of a bend is dangerous for houses? Why?
The outside of the bend is dangerous, because the river erodes the bank there.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the mature stage of a river and the landforms made by lateral erosion and deposition.

qa.q: Give three characteristics of the middle course.
qa.a: The gradient is gentle, the channel is wider and deeper, and the valley is an open V shape with a flat floor.

qa.q: What is the main process in the middle course?
qa.a: Lateral (sideways) erosion widens the valley, and transportation is the main work of the river. Deposition begins on the inside of bends.

qa.q: How does a river carry its load?
qa.a: It rolls big stones (traction), bounces small stones (saltation), carries fine mud (suspension) and carries dissolved minerals (solution).

sum.title: I. Main Characteristics and Processes
sum.intro: The middle course is the mature stage of the river:
items: A. Characteristics
– Gentle gradient.
– Wider and deeper channel with more water.
– Open V-shaped valley with a flat floor.
– Smaller and rounder load.
B. Processes
– Lateral (sideways) erosion widens the valley.
– Transportation is the main work: traction, saltation, suspension and solution.
– Deposition begins on the inside of bends.

qa.q: Study a meander and its cross-section.

qa.a: A meander is a large bend in a river. It forms by erosion on the outside of the bend and deposition on the inside.

qa.q: How does a river cliff form?
qa.a: On the outside of the bend, the water is deep and fast. It erodes the bank by hydraulic action and abrasion and forms a steep river cliff.

qa.q: How does a slip-off slope form?
qa.a: On the inside of the bend, the water is shallow and slow. It deposits sand and gravel, forming a gentle slip-off slope (point bar).

sum.title: II. Landforms of the Middle Course
sum.intro: Lateral erosion and deposition form the following landforms:
items: A. Open V-Shaped Valley
Lateral erosion widens the valley. It has gentle sides and a flat floor.
B. Meanders
A meander is a large bend in a river, formed by erosion on the outside and deposition on the inside of the bend.
meander.png
C. River Cliffs and Slip-Off Slopes
– River cliff: a steep bank on the outside of a bend, where the fast water erodes.
– Slip-off slope (point bar): a gentle bank of sand on the inside of a bend, where the slow water deposits.

evaluation: What is the main process in the middle course?
Lateral erosion, with transportation of the load.
What is the difference between a river cliff and a slip-off slope?
A river cliff is a steep bank eroded on the outside of a bend; a slip-off slope is a gentle bank of deposits on the inside.
How does a river carry fine mud?
It carries fine mud in suspension.
remediation: A large bend in a river is a ______.
The steep bank on the outside of a bend is a river ______.
The gentle bank on the inside of a bend is a ______ slope.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. lateral 2. meander 3. cliff 4. slip-off 5. traction 6. saltation

The four modes of transport were added because transportation is the main work of the river in the middle course.
